The Current Scenario

Bitcoin closed yet another Sunday in the red, testing the psychological support at $65,000 with surgical precision before recovering to $66,010. There were four consecutive bearish closes: Thursday and Friday each dropped -3.51%, Saturday practically flatlined, and Sunday brought another -0.55%.

For those who have been following the analyses here, the trigger is nothing new: the US-Iran War has kept risk-off active since 02/28. The S&P 500 closed Friday down -1.67%, the dollar holds near 100.19, and gold remains the traditional market's preferred safe haven while BTC gives ground.
On the technical front, the picture hasn't improved. BTC is trading below the 50 and 100-week EMAs ($83,300),
bear market confirmed without ambiguity
. The 200-week EMA ($68,200) was lost on 03/26 and has turned into resistance since then, rejecting every recovery attempt this week.

The Fear & Greed Index is at 8 (Extreme Fear), a level of historic capitulation. In previous cycles, readings below 10 marked short-term bottoms. It's no guarantee of a reversal, but it's where long-term buyers have historically started to appear.

The parallel with previous cycles demands attention: In the 2021 cycle, when BTC was in a similar position, the following three months brought the collapse of LUNA and 3AC, taking the price from ~$45,000 to ~$17,000. In 2017, it resulted in a consolidation before the final collapse to $3,200 in December 2018. In both cycles, this phase
did not represent the definitive bottom.
The current BTC is -47.7% from the ATH of $126,200. The historical script suggests caution: the risk of repeating this pattern exists, especially with the
adverse macro context we have today
Bullish Scenario

For the positive scenario to materialize, BTC needs to close on the daily above $68,200, the 200-week EMA, reclaiming the ground lost on 03/26. Closing above $67,500 would already be an intermediate sign of strength.
Three concrete catalysts could change the picture next week:

Powell's speech tomorrow is the most immediate: if the Fed Chair signals openness to rate cuts sooner than expected, the market could interpret it as future liquidity injection and react with risk buying.
On Thursday (04/02), if Trump softens or delays the 'Liberation Day' tariffs, the pressure on risk assets partially eases.

The third catalyst is the least likely but the most impactful: any signal of a formal ceasefire in the US-Iran War. Polymarket prices only a 1.85% chance of a deal by 03/31. Don't expect this, but know that any news in that direction would be a disproportionately positive shock for BTC.
If the bullish scenario confirms, the targets are $68,000 to $70,000.
Bearish Scenario

The bear case is straightforward: a daily close below $65,000. Remember we've been pointing to this level as the immediate line of defense since Friday? Today it was tested, the third test of this region in just a few days. Each retest exhausts the marginal buyers sustaining this support.

The most powerful macro trigger of the week comes on Thursday (04/02): Trump's 'Liberation Day,' with reciprocal tariff announcements. If the tariffs are more aggressive than expected, it could trigger a global sell-off similar to February's, pushing capital toward the dollar and gold.

The combination of an active war with no ceasefire in sight (98.15% probability according to Polymarket) and no Fed cut in April (99.55%) keeps the environment hostile for crypto across all visible time horizons.

Open Interest dropped from ~95,200 to ~93,200 BTC over the past 48 hours while the price also declined — a sign of longs exiting, not aggressive short accumulation. With 68% of accounts still long, a break below $65,000 on the daily close could trigger cascading liquidations.
If $65,000 is lost, the targets are $63,000 to $60,000, near the provisional bottom of February 2026.
What to Watch
Two immediate triggers define the short-term path.

items.text: Powell's speech on Monday (03/30) — the market's reading of the tone will move BTC immediately.
Trump's 'Liberation Day' on Thursday (04/02) — any announcement of tariffs harsher than expected pressures all risk assets simultaneously.
